findings.claim: D-166 says every request that arrives on an open keep-alive connection after STOPPING began gets 503 with Connection: close. On TinyHttpd this holds only until the adapter stop of D-162 starts. From then on, HttpServer.stop calls onServerStopping, which closes idle keep-alive connections without an answer (a request racing the close is dropped with lingerClose), and in-flight responses are committed with Connection: close because isStopping() is true. Later requests on those connections get a closed socket, not a 503. A T44 test written to D-166 as stated would fail or flake.
findings.suggested_fix: Change D-166: requests that reach the dispatcher after STOPPING get 503 with Connection: close. Once the adapter stop has begun, idle keep-alive connections may instead be closed without processing the request. Have the T44 test assert one of these two outcomes.

findings.claim: No item says whether the TinyHttpd adapter sets TinyHttpd's maxRequestBodyBytes (default -1). D-219's mapping of TinyHttpd size-overrun body exceptions to 413 only matters if the limit is set. If it is set, a request whose declared Content-Length is above it gets a fixed plain-text 413 from RequestParser before dispatch. That 413 skips onError, the standard error JSON and the access log, which breaks D-129 (onError receives framework 413 errors), and it is missing from the D-400 list of transport-level rejections.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the adapter leaves maxRequestBodyBytes at -1, so the per-type limits of D-088 apply in the core and TinyHttpd's maxDrainBytes bounds bodies no one reads. If a backstop limit is wanted, set it above every core limit and add the pre-dispatch 413 to D-400 and docs/api/defaults.md.

findings.claim: D-401 reads 'wave 6 adds temporary-file cleanup and wave 7 adds WebSocket closing and SSE closing as before-wait participants', which can be parsed as making temp-file cleanup a before-wait participant. If it runs before the adapter stop, it deletes spool files of uploads still in flight, which D-342 lets complete.
findings.suggested_fix: State that temp-file cleanup (D-255) is a force-close or after-onStop participant.

findings.claim: D-419 makes the WebSocket message limit configurable. TinyHttpd also enforces a separate per-frame limit, maxFramePayloadBytes (default 1 MiB), which closes with 1009. No item maps the configured limit onto it, so raising the message limit above 1 MiB still closes connections that send one large unfragmented frame.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the D-419 setting also set WebSocketHandler.maxFramePayloadBytes to the message limit, or record the frame limit in websocket.md and defaults.md.

findings.claim: D-440 rewrites only the kotlin.md examples. docs/api/README.md and express-migration.md also have Kotlin examples that pass the now-nullable req.body(...) result straight to a service call. Under D-349 these compile only if the test stubs take nullable parameters, so the docs teach passing T? onward.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend D-440 to every docs/api Kotlin example that uses req.body(...), using the reified extension or a null check.

findings.claim: TinyHttpd accepts an asterisk-form 'OPTIONS * HTTP/1.1' and passes the raw path '*' to the handler. No item says how the core treats a raw path that does not start with '/' (reject with 400, or answer server-wide OPTIONS). I-021 requires the same status on every adapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an item fixing the core's answer to asterisk-form OPTIONS, for example 204 with an Allow listing the server's methods, or 400, and include it in the I-021 cases.

findings.claim: CLAUDE.md names only NaruServe-api and NaruServe-servlet as modules and names NaruServe-api as the API 21 check target. D-002 adds seven modules and D-027 extends animal-sniffer to them, but only D-365 (the sample exception) updates CLAUDE.md, so project instructions go stale after wave 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Have wave 1 update the CLAUDE.md module line with the module set and API 21 check targets fixed in #1.

findings.claim: object.md 9.3 requires testing symlink/TOCTOU, but no item covers a path component swapped for a symlink between the canonical check and the open.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an item: re-check the opened file's canonical path after opening (or open, then verify), and record the remaining java.io-only TOCTOU limit in static.md.

findings.claim: The design does not say who renders the HttpExceptions that TinyHttpd's WebSocketHandler.handle and Upgraded.start throw before the 101: 400 for a malformed handshake, 426 with Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13, 403 for Origin or a null listener, 413 when the upgrade body exceeds maxDrainBytes, and 503 with Retry-After when maxUpgradedConnections is reached. If the wave 7 upgrade class lets them propagate, TinyHttpd's ErrorHandler of D-405 renders them with a fresh request id and no access-log line, which contradicts D-430 (a rejected upgrade gets its ordinary D-173 line with the rejection status) and D-135 (requestId equals the access-log id). It can also drop the RFC 6455 4.2.2 Sec-WebSocket-Version header, unless the ErrorHandler copies the exception's headers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an item: the TinyHttpd upgrade class catches every HttpException from WebSocketHandler.handle and res.upgrade before commit and answers it through the dispatcher's own response, with the request's id, the access-log line of D-430 and the exception's headers (Sec-WebSocket-Version, Retry-After) kept. Narrow D-405 to errors raised outside any NaruServe dispatch. Add a T19/T22 test asserting the 426 header and the access line for a rejected upgrade.

findings.claim: Before-wait participants run before the adapter stop, so for up to 1 s (D-435) TinyHttpd keeps accepting connections. Also, a handler already past the STOPPING check can still call res.sse() or reach the upgrade extension point after the SSE and WebSocket closing participants took their snapshot of open streams. Such a late stream gets no closing notice and stays until TinyHttpd aborts it at the deadline. A late WebSocket session finds the sender executor stopped and gets its close(1001) only from TinyHttpd's fireStop on the stopping thread. object.md 11.4 step 2 also orders 'stop accepting new connections/upgrades' before the SSE/WS goodbye of step 3. Nothing says how streams created after a participant ran are handled.
findings.suggested_fix: State that each closing participant first sets a closed flag under the same lock its registry uses. After that, res.sse() fails, or returns a stream that is ended at once with the closing notice, and an upgrade that reaches the extension point is rejected (or closed with 1001 right after the 101) instead of being registered. Also say that accepting new TCP connections during the before-wait phase is allowed because every request is answered 503 under D-166, so the deviation from object.md 11.4 step 2 is on record.

findings.claim: TinyHttpd enforces two separate limits: maxFramePayloadBytes, which also caps an unfragmented message and the first fragment, and maxMessageBytes, which is checked only on continuation frames. Both default to 1 MiB. D-419 makes the WebSocket message limit configurable but maps it to neither setting. If only maxMessageBytes is raised, a single-frame message above 1 MiB still closes with 1009. If only the frame limit is lowered, fragmented messages are still checked against 1 MiB.
findings.suggested_fix: Say in D-419 that the configured message limit is passed to both WebSocketHandler.maxFramePayloadBytes and maxMessageBytes. Add a T20 case with a non-default limit, sent once as one frame and once fragmented.

findings.claim: TinyHttpd accepts 'OPTIONS * HTTP/1.1' and passes requestUri '*' to the handler. The design's raw-path pass-through (D-399), the rejection rules (D-052) and the router results (D-390) all assume a path that starts with '/', so the result for an asterisk-form OPTIONS is undefined, and the in-memory/TinyHttpd parity check of I-021 cannot cover it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one item fixing the dispatcher's answer to OPTIONS * (for example 204 with Allow covering the server-wide methods, or 404/400), applied the same way on both adapters.

findings.claim: The router resolves GET with Upgrade: websocket against WebSocket registrations separately, but no result is defined for an upgrade request to a path that has only a GET route, or no WebSocket route. It is unclear whether this falls back to the GET handler, returns no match (404), or gets a dedicated rejection.
findings.suggested_fix: State the fallback (for example 'an Upgrade request with no WebSocket registration is matched as an ordinary GET') and cover it with a router test.
